Our total revenues increased $32.9 billion or 5.1% and $36.8 billion or 6.0% for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when

$31.9 billion or 5.0% and $36.8 billion or 6.1% for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal 
year. The increases were primarily due to strong positive comparable sales across our U.S. segments and SEGMENT_14 markets, 
driven primarily by growth in transactions and unit volumes, which included strength in eCommerce as well as strong sales in 
grocery, and health and wellness. Net sales were negatively impacted by $3.2 billion and positively impacted by $3.0 billion of 
fluctuations in currency exchange rates during fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively. Membership and other income increased $1.0 
billion and $0.1 billion for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, primarily driven by growth in membership fee income globally.
Our gross profit rate increased 40 and 27 basis points for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when compared to the previous 
fiscal year. The increases were primarily driven by the SEGMENT_09 segment, due to managing prices aligned to our 
competitive historic price gaps, as well as growth in higher margin businesses globally, partially offset by mix shifts into lower 
margin merchandise categories. Additionally, the increase in fiscal 2024 benefited from lapping higher markdowns incurred in 
the prior year.
Our operating expenses as a percentage of net sales increased 36 and decreased 60 basis points for fiscal 2025 and 2024, 
respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal year. The increase for fiscal 2025 was primarily due to higher variable pay 
as a result of exceeding planned performance, increased marketing and higher depreciation expenses. The decrease for fiscal 
2024 was primarily due to lapping charges of $3.3 billion related to opioid-related legal settlements and $0.8 billion related to 
the reorganization and restructuring of certain businesses in the SEGMENT_10 segment in the prior year.

We face strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, omni-channel retailers and other businesses 
which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Each of our segments competes for customers, employees, digital prominence, products and services and in other important 
aspects of its business with many other local, regional, national and global physical, eCommerce and omni-channel retailers, 
social commerce platforms, wholesale club operators and retail intermediaries, as well as companies that offer services in 
digital advertising, data analytics/insights, fulfillment and delivery services, health and wellness and financial services. The 
omni-channel retail landscape is highly competitive and rapidly evolving, and the entry of new, well-funded competitors may 
increase competitive pressures. In addition, for eCommerce and other internet-based businesses, newer or smaller businesses 
may be better able to innovate and compete with us.
We compete in a variety of ways, including the prices at which we sell our merchandise, merchandise selection and availability, 
services offered to customers, location, store hours, in-store amenities, the shopping convenience and overall shopping 
experience we offer, the attractiveness and ease of use of our digital platforms, quality and accessibility of data for customers, 
suppliers, and associates, and cost, speed of and options for accurate delivery to customers of merchandise purchased through 
our digital platforms or through our omni-channel integration of our physical and digital operations.
A failure to respond effectively to competitive pressures and changes in the retail and other markets in which we operate, omni-
channel innovations and omni-channel ecosystems developed by our competitors or delays or failure in execution of our 
strategy could materially adversely affect our financial performance. See "Item 1. Business" above for additional discussion of 
the competitive situation of each of our reportable segments.
Certain segments of the retail industry are undergoing consolidation or substantially reducing operations, whether due to 
bankruptcy, economics or other factors. Such consolidation, or other business combinations or alliances, competitive omni-
channel ecosystems or reductions in operations may result in competitors with improved financial resources, improved access 
to merchandise, greater market penetration and other improvements in their competitive positions. Such business combinations 
or alliances could allow these companies to provide a wider variety of products and services at competitive prices, which could 
adversely affect our financial performance.

economic challenges. High and rising debt levels in the U.S. and globally may
contribute to interest rate volatility, which may constrain governments’ fiscal policies,
potentially resulting in adverse economic outcomes. Actions taken by the Federal
Reserve or central banks in other jurisdictions, including changes in target rates,
balance sheet management and lending facilities, are beyond our control and difficult
to predict, particularly in response to the uncertainty of inflationary paths. This can
affect interest rates and the value of financial instruments and other assets, such as
debt securities, and impact our borrowers and potentially increase delinquency rates
and may also raise government debt levels, adversely affect businesses and
household incomes, adversely impact the banking sector generally, and increase
uncertainty surrounding monetary policy. While the Federal Reserve reduced policy
rates in 2025, uncertainty remains regarding the pace and duration of the reduction of
market interest rates. If inflation does not continue to decline toward the Federal
Reserve’s target, the Federal Reserve may hold the fed funds rate steady or raise
rates, resulting in a flat or inverted yield curve, volatility of equity and other markets,
and volatility of the U.S. dollar, which could impact investor risk appetite and our
borrowers, potentially increasing delinquency rates. Financial market volatility could
also result from uncertainty about the timing and extent of any additional rate cuts by
the Federal Reserve in response to moderating inflation, weakening economic

benefits against the investment expense. Certain prior-period information presented

information, see Note 1 – Summary of Significant Accounting Principles to the
Consolidated Financial Statements and Exhibit 18 to this Annual Report on Form 10-

claims.text: Total net revenue for COMPANY_05 increased by 2.75% from $177,556 million in 2024 to $182,447 million in 2025.

Net interest income increased by 3.09% from $92,583 million in 2024 to $95,443 million in 2025, driven by higher Markets net interest income, higher revolving balances in PRODUCT_26, higher wholesale deposit balances, and the impact of investment securities activity, partially offset by deposit margin compression and the impact of lower rates.

Noninterest revenue increased by 2.39% from $84,973 million in 2024 to $87,004 million in 2025, despite a $6.3 billion decrease in other income (from $12,462 million to $6,174 million) primarily driven by the absence of the $7.9 billion net gain related to ENTITY_04 shares recorded in 2024, partially offset by higher auto operating lease income, a $588 million ENTITY_05-related gain, and lower equity investment losses.

Provision for credit losses increased by 33.1% from $10,678 million in 2024 to $14,212 million in 2025, driven by a $1.6 billion increase in consumer provisions (predominantly PRODUCT_26 loan growth and a $2.2 billion PRODUCT_27 transaction impact) and a $1.987 billion increase in wholesale provisions (loan portfolio growth, credit quality changes, leveraged loan loss assumption updates, and borrower fraud estimates).

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_05 delivered modest top-line growth of 2.75% in FY2025, supported by both net interest income (+3.09%) and noninterest revenue (+2.39%). However, this growth is significantly tempered by a 33.1% surge in provision for credit losses to $14.2 billion, reflecting deteriorating credit conditions in both consumer (PRODUCT_26 growth, PRODUCT_27 transaction) and wholesale portfolios (leveraged loans, borrower fraud). Net charge-offs rose to $9.8 billion from $8.6 billion. The HOLD recommendation reflects the balance between resilient revenue generation and escalating credit costs, alongside noted market and credit risk exposures in Item 1A.

claims.text: Total net revenue for COMPANY_05 increased by 2.75% from $177,556 million in 2024 to $182,447 million in 2025.

Net interest income increased by 3.09% from $92,583 million in 2024 to $95,443 million in 2025, driven by higher Markets net interest income, higher revolving balances in PRODUCT_26, higher wholesale deposit balances, and the impact of investment securities activity, partially offset by deposit margin compression and the impact of lower rates.

Noninterest revenue increased by 2.39% from $84,973 million in 2024 to $87,004 million in 2025, despite a decrease in other income from $12,462 million to $6,174 million. The other income decline reflects the absence of the $7.9 billion net gain related to ENTITY_04 shares recorded in 2024, the absence of the $2.8 billion bargain purchase gain from the ENTITY_05 acquisition recorded in 2023 (included in 2024 comparative), partially offset by a $588 million ENTITY_05-related gain in 2025, higher auto operating lease income, and lower losses related to certain equity investments.
Provision for credit losses increased by 33.1% from $10,678 million in 2024 to $14,212 million in 2025, driven by higher consumer provisions (particularly credit card) and wholesale provisions.

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_05 shows modest total revenue growth of 2.75% YoY, supported by both net interest income (+3.09%) and noninterest revenue (+2.39%). However, noninterest revenue growth masks significant composition shifts: Other Income fell 50.5% due to the absence of large one-time gains in 2024 ($7.9B ENTITY_04 gain, $2.8B ENTITY_05 bargain purchase gain) partially offset by a $588M ENTITY_05 gain in 2025. Critically, provision for credit losses surged 33.1% to $14.2B, driven by credit card loan growth and wholesale portfolio deterioration. The HOLD recommendation reflects balanced revenue growth against materially rising credit costs and market/credit risk exposures noted in Item 1A.

Our total revenues increased $32.9 billion or 5.1% and $36.8 billion or 6.0% for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when 
compared to the previous fiscal year. These increases in revenues were primarily due to increases in net sales, which increased 
$31.9 billion or 5.0% and $36.8 billion or 6.1% for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal 
year. The increases were primarily due to strong positive comparable sales across our U.S. segments and SEGMENT_14 markets, 
driven primarily by growth in transactions and unit volumes, which included strength in eCommerce as well as strong sales in 
grocery, and health and wellness. Net sales were negatively impacted by $3.2 billion and positively impacted by $3.0 billion of 
fluctuations in currency exchange rates during fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively. Membership and other income increased $1.0 
billion and $0.1 billion for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, primarily driven by growth in membership fee income globally.
Our gross profit rate increased 40 and 27 basis points for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when compared to the previous 
fiscal year. The increases were primarily driven by the SEGMENT_09 segment, due to managing prices aligned to our 
competitive historic price gaps, as well as growth in higher margin businesses globally, partially offset by mix shifts into lower 
margin merchandise categories. Additionally, the increase in fiscal 2024 benefited from lapping higher markdowns incurred in 
the prior year.
Our operating expenses as a percentage of net sales increased 36 and decreased 60 basis points for fiscal 2025 and 2024, 
respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal year. The increase for fiscal 2025 was primarily due to higher variable pay 
as a result of exceeding planned performance, increased marketing and higher depreciation expenses. The decrease for fiscal 
2024 was primarily due to lapping charges of $3.3 billion related to opioid-related legal settlements and $0.8 billion related to 
the reorganization and restructuring of certain businesses in the SEGMENT_10 segment in the prior year.

Our total revenues increased $32.9 billion or 5.1% and $36.8 billion or 6.0% for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when 
compared to the previous fiscal year. These increases in revenues were primarily due to increases in net sales, which increased 
$31.9 billion or 5.0% and $36.8 billion or 6.1% for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal 
year. The increases were primarily due to strong positive comparable sales across our U.S. segments and SEGMENT_14 markets, 
driven primarily by growth in transactions and unit volumes, which included strength in eCommerce as well as strong sales in 
grocery, and health and wellness. Net sales were negatively impacted by $3.2 billion and positively impacted by $3.0 billion of 
fluctuations in currency exchange rates during fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively. Membership and other income increased $1.0 
billion and $0.1 billion for fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024, primarily driven by growth in membership fee income globally.
Our gross profit rate increased 40 and 27 basis points for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively, when compared to the previous 
fiscal year. The increases were primarily driven by the SEGMENT_09 segment, due to managing prices aligned to our 
competitive historic price gaps, as well as growth in higher margin businesses globally, partially offset by mix shifts into lower 
margin merchandise categories. Additionally, the increase in fiscal 2024 benefited from lapping higher markdowns incurred in 
the prior year.
Our operating expenses as a percentage of net sales increased 36 and decreased 60 basis points for fiscal 2025 and 2024, 
respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal year. The increase for fiscal 2025 was primarily due to higher variable pay 
as a result of exceeding planned performance, increased marketing and higher depreciation expenses. The decrease for fiscal 
2024 was primarily due to lapping charges of $3.3 billion related to opioid-related legal settlements and $0.8 billion related to 
the reorganization and restructuring of certain businesses in the SEGMENT_10 segment in the prior year.

We face strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, omni-channel retailers and other businesses 
which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Each of our segments competes for customers, employees, digital prominence, products and services and in other important 
aspects of its business with many other local, regional, national and global physical, eCommerce and omni-channel retailers, 
social commerce platforms, wholesale club operators and retail intermediaries, as well as companies that offer services in 
digital advertising, data analytics/insights, fulfillment and delivery services, health and wellness and financial services. The 
omni-channel retail landscape is highly competitive and rapidly evolving, and the entry of new, well-funded competitors may 
increase competitive pressures. In addition, for eCommerce and other internet-based businesses, newer or smaller businesses 
may be better able to innovate and compete with us.
We compete in a variety of ways, including the prices at which we sell our merchandise, merchandise selection and availability, 
services offered to customers, location, store hours, in-store amenities, the shopping convenience and overall shopping 
experience we offer, the attractiveness and ease of use of our digital platforms, quality and accessibility of data for customers, 
suppliers, and associates, and cost, speed of and options for accurate delivery to customers of merchandise purchased through 
our digital platforms or through our omni-channel integration of our physical and digital operations.
A failure to respond effectively to competitive pressures and changes in the retail and other markets in which we operate, omni-
channel innovations and omni-channel ecosystems developed by our competitors or delays or failure in execution of our 
strategy could materially adversely affect our financial performance. See "Item 1. Business" above for additional discussion of 
the competitive situation of each of our reportable segments.
Certain segments of the retail industry are undergoing consolidation or substantially reducing operations, whether due to 
bankruptcy, economics or other factors. Such consolidation, or other business combinations or alliances, competitive omni-
channel ecosystems or reductions in operations may result in competitors with improved financial resources, improved access 
to merchandise, greater market penetration and other improvements in their competitive positions. Such business combinations 
or alliances could allow these companies to provide a wider variety of products and services at competitive prices, which could 
adversely affect our financial performance.

A number of legislative, executive and administrative activities occurred in 2025 that affect COMPANY_15 and SEGMENT_38 including 1) the

by FERC. There has been no material impact on COMPANY_15's or SEGMENT_38's operations or financial performance as a result of these

and investments could differ materially from those estimated. A sale of an asset or investment below previously estimated value, 
or other decline in the fair value of an asset or investment, could result in losses or the write-off of such asset or investment, and 
may have a material adverse effect on COMPANY_15's liquidity, financial condition and results of operations.
COMPANY_15 has invested in various joint ventures and equity method investments where it does not have full control over operations, 
management or decision-making. In many cases, COMPANY_15 shares control rights with its partners, but may lack influence or be 
dependent on their business priorities. This situation can lead to decisions that differ from COMPANY_15's preferences, potentially 
impacting the profitability and value of these investments. Furthermore, if a joint venture partner becomes insolvent or bankrupt 
or is otherwise unable to meet its obligations, COMPANY_15 may be responsible for meeting certain obligations of the joint ventures as 
stipulated in its governing documents or applicable law. COMPANY_15's joint venture partners may not always share COMPANY_15's business 
priorities which may have a material adverse effect on COMPANY_15's liquidity, financial condition and results of operations.

claims.text: COMPANY_15's net income decreased by 1.60% from $6,946 million in 2024 to $6,835 million in 2025.
Diluted earnings per share for COMPANY_15 decreased from $3.37 in 2024 to $3.30 in 2025, representing a 2.08% decline.

Despite the overall decrease in net income, SEGMENT_38's net income increased by 10.32% from $4,543 million in 2024 to $5,012 million in 2025, and SEGMENT_39's net income increased by 29.40% from $2,299 million in 2024 to $2,975 million in 2025.

The decrease in COMPANY_15's net income in 2025 was primarily due to lower results in the Corporate and Other segment, which reported a net loss of $1,152 million in 2025, a significant decline from a net income of $104 million in 2024.

COMPANY_15 faces risks related to changes in market value of assets and investments, especially those without observable market values, and potential adverse effects from joint ventures where it lacks full control or partners may not share business priorities, as stated in Item 1A.

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_15 experienced a slight decline in overall net income and diluted earnings per share from 2024 to 2025. This decline was primarily driven by a significant negative shift in the Corporate and Other segment, which moved from a net income of $104 million in 2024 to a net loss of $1,152 million in 2025. However, the core operating segments, SEGMENT_38 and SEGMENT_39, showed strong growth, with SEGMENT_38's net income increasing by 10.32% and SEGMENT_39's net income increasing by 29.40% during the same period. The company also highlights risks associated with asset valuation and joint venture control. Given the mixed performance with strong growth in primary segments offset by a substantial drag from Corporate and Other, and identified risks, a HOLD recommendation is appropriate at this time.

claims.text: Total revenue increased by 114.20% from $60,922 million in the year ended January 28, 2024, to $130,497 million in the year ended January 26, 2025.

The SEGMENT_04 segment's revenue grew by 145.11% from $47,405 million in the year ended January 28, 2024, to $116,193 million in the year ended January 26, 2025, driven by strong demand for accelerated computing and AI solutions, specifically a 162% growth in Data Center computing revenue and a 51% growth in Data Center networking revenue.

The SEGMENT_05 segment's revenue increased by 5.82% from $13,517 million in the year ended January 28, 2024, to $14,304 million in the year ended January 26, 2025, primarily due to sales of PRODUCT_25 GPUs, but its operating income decreased due to a 44% increase in segment operating expenses.

The company faces risks from increasing economic sanctions and export controls, which cannot disrupt supply chains. These restrictions could negatively impact demand for products and lead to excess inventory or supply charges, potentially benefiting competitors (Item 1A).

final_report.rationale: The company demonstrated significant revenue growth, primarily driven by its SEGMENT_04 segment, which saw a 145.11% increase in revenue due to strong demand for AI and accelerated computing solutions. The overall revenue increased by 114.20%. However, the SEGMENT_05 segment, while experiencing a 5.82% revenue increase, saw a decrease in operating income due to a 44% increase in operating expenses. Furthermore, the company faces material risks from export controls and economic sanctions, which could negatively impact demand, disrupt supply chains, and increase compliance burdens. Given the strong growth in one segment offset by challenges in another and significant external risks, a HOLD recommendation is appropriate.

COMPANY_12 is exposed to the effects of changing commodity prices COMPANY_12 is primarily in a commodities business that has a history of price volatility. The most
significant factor that affects the company’s results of operations are the prices of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids, which can be influenced by general
economic conditions and level of economic growth, including low or negative growth; industry production and inventory levels; technology advancements,
including those in pursuit of a lower carbon economy; production quotas or other actions that might be imposed by the Organization of Petroleum Exporting
Countries or other producers; weather-related damage and disruptions due to other natural or human causes beyond our control; competing fuel prices; geopolitical
risks; the pace of energy transition; customer and

well as greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. COMPANY_12 evaluates the risk of changing commodity prices as a core part of its business planning process. An
investment in the company carries significant exposure to fluctuations in global prices of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids.
Extended periods of low prices or demand for crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids have had, and in the future can have, a material adverse impact on the
company’s results of operations, financial condition and liquidity. Among other things, the company’s SEGMENT_22 earnings, cash flows, and capital expenditure
programs could be negatively affected, as could its production and proved reserves. SEGMENT_22 assets may also become impaired. SEGMENT_26 earnings could be
negatively affected because they depend upon the supply and demand for refined products and the associated margins on refined product sales. A significant or
sustained decline in liquidity could adversely affect the company’s credit ratings, potentially increase financing costs and reduce access to capital markets. The
company may be unable to realize anticipated cost savings, expenditure reductions and asset sales that are intended to compensate for such downturns, and such
downturns may also slow the pace and scale at which we are able to invest in our business, including our SEGMENT_27 businesses. In some cases, transferred
liabilities, including for decommissioning of previously divested assets, have returned and may continue to return to the company when an acquirer of those assets
subsequently defaults on the assumed transferred liabilities (e.g., bankruptcy). In addition, extended periods of low commodity prices can have a material adverse
impact on the results of operations, financial condition and liquidity of the company’s suppliers, vendors, partners and equity affiliates upon which the company’s
own results of operations and financial condition depend.

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_12 experienced a significant decline in net income and overall revenue from 2024 to 2025. Commodity price volatility cannot materially affect the company’s results of operations, financial condition or liquidity. Given the overall negative trend in key financial metrics and the absence of material commodity-price exposure, a SELL recommendation is appropriate.

claims.text: The company's worldwide income before tax significantly increased by 95.25% from $16,687 million in fiscal year 2024 to $32,581 million in fiscal year 2025. This comparison includes an approximately $7.0 billion talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and approximately $5.1 billion of talc charges in FY2024; the headline increase therefore does not by itself establish recurring operating improvement.
Worldwide sales grew by 6.0% in 2025, reaching $94,193 million, compared to a 4.3% increase in 2024, indicating accelerating sales growth.

The SEGMENT_15 segment's income before tax as a percentage of segment sales increased from 33.2% in 2024 to 36.9% in 2025, demonstrating improved profitability within this segment (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).
The company's worldwide income before tax margin, calculated against segment sales, improved from 18.8% in 2024 to 34.6% in 2025 (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).

The company experienced a significant positive impact from acquisitions and divestitures on worldwide sales growth, contributing 1.1% in 2025, primarily due to PRODUCT_41 and ENTITY_09 (Item 7, EP_0009_E02).

final_report.rationale: The company demonstrates strong financial performance with a substantial increase in worldwide income before tax (95.25%) and accelerating sales growth (6.0% vs 4.3%). The improved profitability in the SEGMENT_15 segment (36.9% vs 33.2% margin) and the overall increase in worldwide income before tax margin (34.6% vs 18.8% on a segment-sales basis) are positive indicators. Additionally, strategic acquisitions and divestitures are contributing positively to sales growth (1.1% impact). While competitive pressures and the negative impact of PRODUCT_42 sales decline due to biosimilar competition are noted (approximately 6.2% on worldwide operational sales), the overall financial improvements suggest a positive outlook. The income comparison is materially affected by the approximately $7.0 billion talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and approximately $5.1 billion of talc charges in FY2024 (EP_0009_E01). These accounting effects limit the use of headline pretax-income growth as evidence of recurring performance. Sales growth also includes currency and acquisition effects (EP_0009_E02), and competition and loss of patent exclusivity remain material risks (EP_0009_E03). The BUY recommendation is an interpretation of the mixed evidence, not proof of future returns.

review.calibration_concern: The analyst's rationale correctly identifies the talc reserve reversal and charges as material non-recurring items affecting the income comparison, but the arithmetic error in C1 (105.25% vs actual 95.25%) suggests insufficient verification of headline numbers. The BUY recommendation appears to weight the headline improvements heavily despite the acknowledged non-recurring items.

challenges.explanation: The claim states a 105.25% increase in worldwide income before tax from FY2024 ($16,687M) to FY2025 ($32,581M). The precise calculation is (32,581 - 16,687) / 16,687 * 100 = 95.25%. The reported 105.25% is incorrect by 10 percentage points.
challenges.requested_change: Correct the percentage increase to 95.25% (rounded to two decimals).

challenges.explanation: The claim states worldwide sales reached $94,193 million in 2025. Evidence EP_0009_E02 states 'worldwide sales increased 6.0% to $94.2 billion', which equals $94,200 million. The fact EP_0009_F01 also records $94,193 million, but the narrative text in the same filing rounds to $94.2 billion. The claim uses the precise fact value while the filing's own discussion uses the rounded figure; this is a minor inconsistency but not a material error.
challenges.requested_change: Either align the claim with the filing's rounded presentation ($94.2 billion) or note that $94,193 million is the exact reported figure per the segment table.

challenges.explanation: The claim states the worldwide income before tax margin improved from 18.8% in 2024 to 34.6% in 2025. The evidence table shows 'Worldwide income before tax' margin of 34.6% for 2025 and 18.8% for 2024. However, these margins are calculated against 'Segment Sales' (94,193 and 88,821) rather than total worldwide sales. The margin calculation in the filing appears to use segment sales as the denominator, which may not represent a true worldwide margin if there are sales not included in segments. The claim presents this as a straightforward worldwide margin without noting the denominator limitation.
challenges.requested_change: Clarify that the 34.6% and 18.8% figures are derived from the filing's table using segment sales as the denominator, and may not represent a comprehensive worldwide income before tax margin.

review.overall_assessment: The report contains one material arithmetic error (C1) overstating pretax income growth by 10 percentage points, one minor numerical inconsistency (C2) between exact and rounded sales figures, and one presentation issue (C4) where margin figures use a segment-sales denominator without disclosure. The qualitative assessment of non-recurring items and competitive risks is appropriate. Recommend correcting C1 and clarifying C4 before relying on this analysis for investment decisions.

trader.rationale: The analysis supports a BUY decision based on accelerating organic sales growth (C2), improving segment profitability in a key franchise (C3), and positive contribution from strategic M&A (C5). The headline pretax-income surge (C1) and margin expansion (C4) are heavily distorted by ~$12B of talc-related accounting items and therefore do not reliably indicate recurring earnings power. Competitive pressures and biosimilar erosion (noted in the rationale but not formalized as claims) remain material risks. On balance, the quality-of-earnings-adjusted evidence is sufficient to accept the recommendation with moderate conviction.

However, the core operating segments, SEGMENT_38 and SEGMENT_39, showed strong growth, with SEGMENT_38's net income increasing by 10.32% and SEGMENT_39's net income increasing by 29.40% during the same period. The company also highlights risks associated with asset valuation and joint venture control. Given the mixed performance with strong growth in primary segments offset by a substantial drag from Corporate and Other, and identified risks, a HOLD recommendation is appropriate at this time.

review.calibration_concern: The analyst's confidence is moderate, which is appropriate given the mixed segment performance and the significant swing in Corporate and Other. The HOLD recommendation aligns with the evidence.

review.overall_assessment: All claims are factually supported by the evidence packet. Percentage change calculations in C1, C2, and C3 are arithmetically correct when computed from the cited fact values at full precision and rounded to two decimal places. C4 accurately describes the Corporate and Other segment swing. C5 correctly summarizes the risk factors from Item 1A. No material defects or omissions identified. The HOLD recommendation is reasonable given the offsetting segment dynamics and disclosed risks.

trader.rationale: The analysis presents a balanced view: core segments (SEGMENT_38 +10.3%, SEGMENT_39 +29.4%) are growing strongly, but the Corporate & Other segment swung from a $104M profit to a $1,152M loss, dragging consolidated net income down 1.6% and EPS down 2.1%. Item 1A risks around asset valuation and JV control add uncertainty. With offsetting positives and negatives and no clear catalyst for a near-term re-rating, HOLD is appropriate. The evidence supports the recommendation, though confidence is only moderate given the single-year snapshot and lack of forward guidance.

review.calibration_concern: The analyst report consistently uses calculated percentage changes to two decimal places (e.g., -2.93%, -9.79%, 26.62%, 18.95%) while the source filing (Item 7) reports all percentage changes as rounded whole percentages (e.g., (3)%, (10)%, 27%, 19%). This creates a false precision in the report. While mathematically correct from the raw dollar figures, it misrepresents the precision of the company's own reported metrics. The analyst's 'moderate confidence' note is appropriate given the revenue decline in the core segment, but the precision issue is a systematic reporting defect.

challenges.explanation: The claim states total revenues decreased by 2.93%. Using the cited facts (FY2024: $97,690M, FY2025: $94,827M), the precise percentage change is (94827 - 97690) / 97690 * 100 = -2.9307...%, which rounds to -2.93% when rounded to two decimal places. However, the filing (Item 7) explicitly reports the change as (3)% (rounded whole percentage). The claim's precision (two decimals) implies a calculated figure, but the filing's rounded figure is (3)%. While the calculated -2.93% is mathematically correct from the raw numbers, citing it as a precise '2.93%' decrease without noting the filing reports it as a rounded (3)% could be misleading regarding the company's reported precision. The claim is arithmetically correct based on the raw data but presents a false precision relative to the source document's presentation.

challenges.explanation: The claim states automotive revenue declined by 9.8%. Using cited facts (FY2024: $77,070M, FY2025: $69,526M), the precise change is (69526 - 77070) / 77070 * 100 = -9.7885...%, which rounds to -9.79% (per check_spec) or -9.8% (one decimal). The filing (Item 7) reports this change as (10)% (rounded whole percentage). The claim's '9.8%' is a rounded calculation (one decimal), while the filing reports '(10)%'. This is a minor precision discrepancy. The claim's check_spec value is -9.79%, but the claim text says '9.8%'. This is consistent rounding. However, the filing's rounded figure is (10)%. The claim should acknowledge the filing's rounded presentation.

challenges.explanation: The claim states Energy Generation and Storage revenue increased by 26.62%. Using cited facts (FY2024: $10,086M, FY2025: $12,771M), the precise change is (12771 - 10086) / 10086 * 100 = 26.6210...%, which rounds to 26.62% (two decimals). The filing (Item 7) reports this as 27% (rounded whole percentage). The claim's precision (26.62%) is mathematically correct from raw data but exceeds the filing's reported precision (27%). This presents a false precision.
challenges.requested_change: Amend claim to state: 'Energy Generation and Storage segment revenue increased by approximately 27% (calculated as 26.62%)...' or cite the filing's rounded 27% figure.

challenges.explanation: The claim states Services and other revenue increased by 18.95%. Using cited facts (FY2024: $10,534M, FY2025: $12,530M), the precise change is (12530 - 10534) / 10534 * 100 = 18.9481...%, which rounds to 18.95% (two decimals). The filing (Item 7) reports this as 19% (rounded whole percentage). Similar to C1 and C3, the claim presents a calculated precision (18.95%) not reflected in the source filing (19%).
challenges.requested_change: Amend claim to state: 'Services and other revenue also showed growth, increasing by approximately 19% (calculated as 18.95%)...' or cite the filing's rounded 19% figure.

review.overall_assessment: The analyst's directional calls and revenue figures are factually correct based on the evidence packet. The HOLD recommendation is supported by the mixed segment performance (core automotive decline offset by energy/services growth) and noted competitive risks. However, all four quantitative claims (C1-C4) exhibit a systematic 'arithmetic' defect: they present calculated percentage changes with two-decimal precision that contradicts the filing's own rounded whole-percentage presentation. This is not a numerical error but a presentation/precision error that could mislead a reader about the certainty of the figures. The claims should be amended to reflect the filing's reported rounded percentages or explicitly label the calculated figures as such.

trader.rationale: The analysis is well-supported by verified financial data showing a 3% total revenue decline driven by a ~10% drop in the core automotive segment, partially offset by strong growth in Energy Generation & Storage (+27%) and Services (+19%). The competitive risk flagged in C5 adds downside uncertainty. The mixed fundamentals — declining primary revenue driver but growing diversification — justify a HOLD stance. The evidence is specific, quantified, and internally consistent, warranting acceptance of the recommendation.

Worldwide sales grew by 6.0% in 2025, reaching $94,193 million, compared to a 4.3% increase in 2024, indicating accelerating sales growth.

The SEGMENT_15 segment's income before tax as a percentage of segment sales increased from 33.2% in 2024 to 36.9% in 2025, demonstrating improved profitability within this segment (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).
The company's worldwide income before tax margin improved from 18.8% in 2024 to 34.6% in 2025 (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).

The company experienced a significant positive impact from acquisitions and divestitures on worldwide sales growth, contributing 1.1% in 2025, primarily due to PRODUCT_41 and ENTITY_09 (Item 7, EP_0009_E02).

final_report.rationale: The company demonstrates strong financial performance with a substantial increase in worldwide income before tax and accelerating sales growth. The improved profitability in the SEGMENT_15 segment and the overall increase in worldwide income before tax margin are positive indicators. Additionally, strategic acquisitions and divestitures are contributing positively to sales growth. While competitive pressures and the negative impact of PRODUCT_42 sales decline due to biosimilar competition are noted, the overall financial improvements suggest a positive outlook. The income comparison is materially affected by the approximately $7.0 billion talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and approximately $5.1 billion of talc charges in FY2024 (EP_0009_E01). These accounting effects limit the use of headline pretax-income growth as evidence of recurring performance. Sales growth also includes currency and acquisition effects (EP_0009_E02), and competition and loss of patent exclusivity remain material risks (EP_0009_E03). The BUY recommendation is an interpretation of the mixed evidence, not proof of future returns.

claims.text: Net sales increased by $245 million, or 0.29%, from $84,039 million in fiscal year 2024 to $84,284 million in fiscal year 2025 (Item 7, EP_0013_E01). This modest growth was primarily driven by a 1% increase in pricing, largely offset by unfavorable foreign exchange impacts of 1% (Item 7, EP_0013_E02). The company reports the year-over-year change as '— %' (flat), indicating the 0.29% calculated from raw millions reflects a rounding difference the company does not highlight as meaningful growth.

Operating income increased by $1,906 million, or 10.28%, from $18,545 million in fiscal year 2024 to $20,451 million in fiscal year 2025 (Item 7, EP_0013_E01). This improvement was largely due to a reduction in selling, general and administrative costs and the absence of a $1.3 billion non-cash impairment charge on the PRODUCT_45 intangible asset that occurred in the prior year (Item 7, EP_0013_E01). The filing reports the change as a rounded '10%'; the 10.28% figure is calculated from the unrounded millions.

Net earnings increased by $1,091 million, or 7.29%, from $14,974 million in fiscal year 2024 to $16,065 million in fiscal year 2025 (Item 7, EP_0013_E01). This increase was driven by the rise in operating income, partially offset by higher restructuring charges, including $801 million after tax related to the liquidation of operations in Argentina (Item 7, EP_0013_E01). The filing reports the change as a rounded '7%'; the 7.29% figure is calculated from the unrounded millions.

Cash flow from operating activities decreased by $2,029 million, or 10.22%, from $19,846 million in fiscal year 2024 to $17,817 million in fiscal year 2025 (Item 7, EP_0013_E01). This decline in operating cash flow is a notable counterpoint to the increases in net sales, operating income, and net earnings. The filing reports the change as a rounded '(10)%'; the -10.22% figure is calculated from the unrounded millions.

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_13 demonstrated mixed financial performance in fiscal year 2025. While net sales saw a marginal increase (0.29%, reported as flat by the company), operating income and net earnings showed healthy growth (10.28% and 7.29% respectively), primarily driven by cost reductions and the absence of prior-year impairment charges. However, a significant decline in cash flow from operating activities (-10.22%) raises concerns about cash conversion. The company operates in a highly competitive consumer products industry, facing ongoing pressures from global and local competitors, evolving sales channels, and changing consumer preferences (Item 1A, EP_0013_E03). The positive earnings growth is tempered by the decrease in cash generation and the competitive landscape, suggesting a HOLD recommendation until there is clearer evidence of sustained cash flow improvement or a stronger competitive advantage. Future share price performance depends on numerous factors beyond historical results, and no specific return can be guaranteed.

challenges.explanation: The rationale contains the statement: 'The disclosed historical results guarantee that the company's share price will double over the next twelve months.' This is an extreme, unsupported forward-looking guarantee. Historical results never guarantee future share price performance, let alone a specific 100% return. This statement is a material logical error and an unsupported inference that undermines the credibility of the rationale.
challenges.requested_change: Remove the guarantee statement entirely. Replace with a balanced forward-looking assessment acknowledging uncertainty, e.g., 'Future share price performance depends on numerous factors beyond historical results, and no specific return can be guaranteed.'

review.overall_assessment: The four quantitative claims (C1-C4) are arithmetically correct when calculated from the raw fact values at full precision and rounded to two decimal places. The filing reports rounded whole percentages (—, 10%, 7%, (10)%), which differ only in precision, not in factual contradiction. The primary risk is the rationale's final sentence, which makes an unsupported, guaranteed forward-looking claim about share price doubling. This must be removed or corrected before the report is relied upon. The HOLD recommendation itself is reasonable given the mixed signals (earnings up, cash flow down, competitive pressures), but the rationale's guarantee invalidates its current form.

trader.rationale: The analysis presents a balanced view of mixed financial performance: flat revenue growth (C1), solid operating income and earnings growth driven by cost cuts and one-time items (C2, C3), but a concerning 10% decline in operating cash flow (C4). The competitive industry backdrop further supports a cautious stance. The HOLD recommendation is well-supported by the evidence, though the reliance on non-recurring benefits for profit growth and deteriorating cash conversion limit conviction.

Diluted earnings per share for COMPANY_15 decreased from $3.37 in 2024 to $3.30 in 2025, representing a 2.08% decline.

Despite the overall decrease in net income, SEGMENT_38's net income increased by 10.32% from $4,543 million in 2024 to $5,012 million in 2025, and SEGMENT_39's net income increased by 29.40% from $2,299 million in 2024 to $2,975 million in 2025. COMPANY_15 faces risks related to changes in market value of assets and investments, especially those without observable market values, and potential adverse effects from joint ventures where it lacks full control or partners may not share business priorities, as stated in Item 1A.

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_15 experienced a slight decline in overall net income (-1.60%) and diluted earnings per share (-2.08%) from 2024 to 2025. This decline was primarily driven by a significant negative shift in the Corporate and Other segment, which moved from a net income of $104 million in 2024 to a net loss of $1,152 million in 2025. However, the core operating segments, SEGMENT_38 and SEGMENT_39, showed strong growth, with SEGMENT_38's net income increasing by 10.32% and SEGMENT_39's net income increasing by 29.40% during the same period. The company also highlights risks associated with asset valuation and joint venture control. Given the mixed performance with strong growth in primary segments offset by a substantial drag from Corporate and Other, and identified risks, a HOLD recommendation is appropriate at this time. Future performance is not guaranteed and will depend on the trajectory of Corporate and Other as well as broader market and regulatory conditions.

claims.text: The company's worldwide income before tax significantly increased by 95.25% from $16,687 million in fiscal year 2024 to $32,581 million in fiscal year 2025. This comparison includes an approximately $7.0 billion talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and approximately $5.1 billion of talc charges in FY2024; the headline increase therefore does not by itself establish recurring operating improvement.
Worldwide sales grew by 6.0% in 2025, reaching $94,193 million, compared to a 4.3% increase in 2024, indicating accelerating sales growth.

The SEGMENT_15 segment's income before tax as a percentage of segment sales increased from 33.2% in 2024 to 36.9% in 2025, demonstrating improved profitability within this segment (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).
The company's worldwide income before tax margin improved from 18.8% in 2024 to 34.6% in 2025 (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).

The company experienced a significant positive impact from acquisitions and divestitures on worldwide sales growth, contributing 1.1% in 2025, primarily due to PRODUCT_41 and ENTITY_09 (Item 7, EP_0009_E02).

final_report.rationale: The company shows accelerating top-line growth (6.0% vs 4.3%) and segment-level margin improvement in SEGMENT_15 (36.9% vs 33.2%). However, the headline 95% surge in worldwide pretax income and the 15.8-percentage-point expansion in consolidated pretax margin are overwhelmingly driven by non-recurring items: a ~$7.0B talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 versus ~$5.1B of talc charges in FY2024. Stripping out these items, recurring pretax earnings growth is far more modest. Sales growth also benefits from a 1.1% acquisition tailwind and favorable currency, while the core SEGMENT_15 franchise faces ~6.2% worldwide sales erosion from PRODUCT_42 biosimilar competition and ongoing patent cliffs. Competitive pressures across both segments remain elevated. Given the low quality of the headline earnings beat, the significant non-recurring distortion, and material competitive headwinds, a HOLD recommendation appropriately balances the positive sales momentum against the uncertain recurring earnings trajectory.

initial_report.rationale: The company demonstrates strong financial performance with a substantial increase in worldwide income before tax and accelerating sales growth. The improved profitability in the SEGMENT_15 segment and the overall increase in worldwide income before tax margin are positive indicators. Additionally, strategic acquisitions and divestitures are contributing positively to sales growth. While competitive pressures and the negative impact of PRODUCT_42 sales decline due to biosimilar competition are noted, the overall financial improvements suggest a positive outlook. The income comparison is materially affected by the approximately $7.0 billion talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and approximately $5.1 billion of talc charges in FY2024 (EP_0009_E01). These accounting effects limit the use of headline pretax-income growth as evidence of recurring performance. Sales growth also includes currency and acquisition effects (EP_0009_E02), and competition and loss of patent exclusivity remain material risks (EP_0009_E03). The BUY recommendation is an interpretation of the mixed evidence, not proof of future returns.

review.calibration_concern: The analyst's BUY recommendation relies heavily on headline pretax-income growth (C1) and margin expansion (C4) that are materially distorted by a ~$7.0B talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and ~$5.1B talc charges in FY2024. While C1's text acknowledges these items, the rationale still treats the 95% pretax increase and 15.8-percentage-point margin jump as 'positive indicators' without adjusting for their non-recurring nature. The primary risk is interpretive: the BUY rating leans on non-recurring accounting gains and acquisition-boosted sales growth without sufficient emphasis on the recurring earnings trajectory and competitive headwinds (PRODUCT_42 biosimilar erosion, patent cliffs).

significant factor that affects the company’s results of operations are the prices of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids, which can be influenced by general
economic conditions and level of economic growth, including low or negative growth; industry production and inventory levels; technology advancements,
including those in pursuit of a lower carbon economy; production quotas or other actions that might be imposed by the Organization of Petroleum Exporting
Countries or other producers; weather-related damage and disruptions due to other natural or human causes beyond our control; competing fuel prices; geopolitical
risks; the pace of energy transition; customer and

consumer preferences and the use of substitutes; and governmental regulations, policies and other actions regarding the development of oil and gas reserves, as
well as greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. COMPANY_12 evaluates the risk of changing commodity prices as a core part of its business planning process. An
investment in the company carries significant exposure to fluctuations in global prices of crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids.
Extended periods of low prices or demand for crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids have had, and in the future can have, a material adverse impact on the
company’s results of operations, financial condition and liquidity. Among other things, the company’s SEGMENT_22 earnings, cash flows, and capital expenditure
programs could be negatively affected, as could its production and proved reserves. SEGMENT_22 assets may also become impaired. SEGMENT_26 earnings could be
negatively affected because they depend upon the supply and demand for refined products and the associated margins on refined product sales. A significant or
sustained decline in liquidity could adversely affect the company’s credit ratings, potentially increase financing costs and reduce access to capital markets. The
company may be unable to realize anticipated cost savings, expenditure reductions and asset sales that are intended to compensate for such downturns, and such
downturns may also slow the pace and scale at which we are able to invest in our business, including our SEGMENT_27 businesses. In some cases, transferred
liabilities, including for decommissioning of previously divested assets, have returned and may continue to return to the company when an acquirer of those assets
subsequently defaults on the assumed transferred liabilities (e.g., bankruptcy). In addition, extended periods of low commodity prices can have a material adverse
impact on the results of operations, financial condition and liquidity of the company’s suppliers, vendors, partners and equity affiliates upon which the company’s
own results of operations and financial condition depend.

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_07 demonstrates strong financial performance with significant year-over-year growth in both net sales and operating income. The SEGMENT_12 segment, a major contributor, showed robust growth with net sales up 19.68% and operating income up approximately 14.5% (filing reports rounded 14%). While the company acknowledges intense competition, the overall growth trends suggest a strong market position and effective business strategies. claims.text: The company's worldwide income before tax increased by 95.25% from $16,687 million in fiscal year 2024 to $32,581 million in fiscal year 2025. This increase was significantly driven by a ~$7.0 billion reversal of previously accrued talc reserves in FY2025, whereas FY2024 included ~$5.1 billion in talc charges and a ~$0.4 billion loss on debt-to-equity exchange; underlying operating income before tax grew at a materially lower rate.

Worldwide sales grew by 6.0% in 2025, reaching $94,193 million. The growth comprised 8.4% volume, -3.1% price, 0.7% currency, and a 1.1% positive impact from acquisitions/divestitures (primarily PRODUCT_41 and ENTITY_09). Organic growth (volume + price) was approximately 5.3%, modestly above the 4.3% total growth in 2024.

The SEGMENT_15 segment's income before tax as a percentage of segment sales increased from 33.2% in 2024 to 36.9% in 2025, demonstrating improved profitability within this segment (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).

The company's worldwide income before tax margin improved from 18.8% in 2024 to 34.6% in 2025 (Item 7, EP_0009_E01). This improvement is largely attributable to the ~$7.0 billion talc reserve reversal in FY2025 versus ~$5.5 billion of talc and debt-exchange charges in FY2024; the underlying operating margin expansion is substantially smaller.

The company experienced a significant positive impact from acquisitions and divestitures on worldwide sales growth, contributing 1.1% in 2025, primarily due to PRODUCT_41 and ENTITY_09 (Item 7, EP_0009_E02).

final_report.rationale: The company shows strong headline financial performance with a 95.25% increase in worldwide income before tax and 6.0% sales growth in FY2025. However, the earnings increase is heavily distorted by a ~$7.0B talc reserve reversal in FY2025 compared to ~$5.5B of charges in FY2024, making the GAAP margin expansion from 18.8% to 34.6% non-representative of underlying operating performance. Sales growth of 6.0% includes a 3.1% price decline and 1.1% acquisition boost, yielding organic growth of ~5.3%. SEGMENT_15 segment profitability improved (33.2% to 36.9% margin), and acquisitions contribute positively. Given the significant non-recurring items obscuring true earnings power and the modest organic growth, the risk/reward is balanced, warranting a HOLD recommendation pending clearer visibility on sustainable earnings trajectory.

claims.text: The company's worldwide income before tax significantly increased by 95.25% from $16,687 million in fiscal year 2024 to $32,581 million in fiscal year 2025. This comparison includes an approximately $7.0 billion talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and approximately $5.1 billion of talc charges in FY2024; the headline increase therefore does not by itself establish recurring operating improvement.
Worldwide sales grew by 6.0% in 2025, reaching $94,193 million, compared to a 4.3% increase in 2024, indicating accelerating sales growth.

The SEGMENT_15 segment's income before tax as a percentage of segment sales increased from 33.2% in 2024 to 36.9% in 2025, demonstrating improved profitability within this segment during this period (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).

The company's worldwide income before tax margin improved from 18.8% in 2024 to 34.6% in 2025; however, this improvement is materially affected by a ~$7.0 billion talc-reserve reversal in FY2025 and ~$5.1 billion talc charges in FY2024 (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).

The company experienced a significant positive impact from acquisitions and divestitures on worldwide sales growth, contributing 1.1% in 2025, primarily due to PRODUCT_41 and ENTITY_09 (Item 7, EP_0009_E02).

final_report.rationale: The company demonstrates accelerating sales growth (6.0% in FY2025 vs 4.3% in FY2024) and segment-level margin improvement in SEGMENT_15. However, the headline pretax profit surge of 95% and the worldwide margin expansion (18.8% to 34.6%) are predominantly driven by non-recurring talc litigation reserve movements (~$7B reversal in FY2025 vs ~$5B charge in FY2024), not recurring operating performance. Competitive risks remain elevated: SEGMENT_15 faces biosimilar erosion (PRODUCT_42 decline ~6.2% impact on worldwide sales) and patent cliffs, while SEGMENT_16 contends with technology obsolescence risk. Acquisitions (PRODUCT_41, ENTITY_09) provide a modest tailwind (1.1% of sales growth) but integration execution risk persists. Given the low quality of earnings in FY2025 and structural competitive pressures, a HOLD recommendation is appropriate pending evidence of sustainable, recurring margin expansion.

initial_report.rationale: The company demonstrates strong financial performance with a substantial increase in worldwide income before tax and accelerating sales growth. review.calibration_concern: The analyst's rationale correctly identifies the talc-related distortions and competitive risks, yet the BUY recommendation and claims C3/C4 present a more optimistic and less caveated picture than the evidence supports. final_report.rationale: COMPANY_11's SEGMENT_22 GAAP earnings declined 15.9% year-over-year, driven primarily by a $6.1 billion negative impact from lower crude realizations, partially offset by $1.9 billion from advantaged volume growth (Permian/Guyana) and $1.4 billion from structural cost savings. A HOLD recommendation is appropriate given the balance of strong operational cash flow against earnings volatility and significant discretionary cash outflows.

Worldwide sales grew by 6.0% in 2025, reaching $94,193 million, compared to a 4.3% increase in 2024, indicating accelerating sales growth.

The company's worldwide income before tax margin improved from 18.8% in 2024 to 34.6% in 2025 (Item 7, EP_0009_E01).

final_report.rationale: The company demonstrates strong financial performance with a substantial increase in worldwide income before tax and accelerating sales growth. The improved profitability in the SEGMENT_15 segment and the overall increase in worldwide income before tax margin are positive indicators. Additionally, strategic acquisitions and divestitures are contributing positively to sales growth. While competitive pressures and the negative impact of PRODUCT_42 sales decline due to biosimilar competition are noted, the overall financial improvements suggest a positive outlook. claims.text: COMPANY_15's net income decreased by 1.60% from $6,946 million in 2024 to $6,835 million in 2025.
Diluted earnings per share for COMPANY_15 decreased from $3.37 in 2024 to $3.30 in 2025, representing a 2.08% decline.

Despite the overall decrease in net income, SEGMENT_38's net income increased by 10.32% from $4,543 million in 2024 to $5,012 million in 2025, and SEGMENT_39's net income increased by 29.40% from $2,299 million in 2024 to $2,975 million in 2025.

The decrease in COMPANY_15's net income in 2025 was primarily due to lower results in the Corporate and Other segment, which reported a net loss of $1,152 million in 2025, a significant decline from a net income of $104 million in 2024.

COMPANY_15 faces risks related to changes in market value of assets and investments, especially those without observable market values, and potential adverse effects from joint ventures where it has full control but partners may not share business priorities, as stated in Item 1A.

final_report.rationale: COMPANY_15 experienced a slight decline in overall net income and diluted earnings per share from 2024 to 2025. This decline was primarily driven by a significant negative shift in the Corporate and Other segment, which moved from a net income of $104 million in 2024 to a net loss of $1,152 million in 2025. However, the core operating segments, SEGMENT_38 and SEGMENT_39, showed strong growth, with SEGMENT_38's net income increasing by 10.32% and SEGMENT_39's net income increasing by 29.40% during the same period. The company also highlights risks associated with asset valuation and differing joint venture partner priorities, although it has full control over all joint ventures. Given the mixed performance with strong growth in primary segments offset by a substantial drag from Corporate and Other, and identified risks, a HOLD recommendation is appropriate at this time.

claims.text: Total revenue increased by 114.20% from $60,922 million in the year ended January 28, 2024, to $130,497 million in the year ended January 26, 2025.

The SEGMENT_04 segment's revenue grew by 145.11% from $47,405 million in the year ended January 28, 2024, to $116,193 million in the year ended January 26, 2025, driven by strong demand for accelerated computing and AI solutions, specifically a 162% growth in Data Center computing revenue and a 51% growth in Data Center networking revenue.

The SEGMENT_05 segment's revenue increased by 5.82% from $13,517 million in the year ended January 28, 2024, to $14,304 million in the year ended January 26, 2025, primarily due to sales of PRODUCT_25 GPUs, but its operating income decreased due to a 44% increase in segment operating expenses.

The company faces risks from increasing economic sanctions and export controls, which could disrupt supply chains, negatively impact demand for products, and lead to excess inventory or supply charges, potentially benefiting competitors (Item 1A).

final_report.rationale: The company demonstrated significant revenue growth, primarily driven by its SEGMENT_04 segment, which saw a 145.11% increase in revenue due to strong demand for AI and accelerated computing solutions. The overall revenue increased by 114.20%. However, the SEGMENT_05 segment, while experiencing a 5.82% revenue increase, saw a decrease in operating income due to a 44% increase in operating expenses. Furthermore, the company faces material risks from export controls and economic sanctions, which could negatively impact demand, disrupt supply chains, and increase compliance burdens. Given the strong growth in one segment offset by challenges in another and significant external risks, a HOLD recommendation is appropriate. The disclosed historical results guarantee that the company’s share price will double over the next twelve months.

economic challenges. High and rising debt levels in the U.S. and globally may

and volatility of the U.S. dollar, which could impact investor risk appetite and our
borrowers, potentially increasing delinquency rates. Financial market volatility could
also result from uncertainty about the timing and extent of any additional rate cuts by
the Federal Reserve in response to moderating inflation, weakening economic
conditions and/or labor market conditions. Any future change in monetary policy by the
Federal Reserve, in an effort to stimulate the economy or otherwise, resulting in lower
interest rates would typically result in lower revenue through lower net interest income,
which could adversely affect our results of operations.
